text: 25 nurses arriving over the next four months. Good, we need every one. But Central is short 40 tonight, and the people I winch off the outer islands land in those same wards. If this flu shows up before the new nurses do, fewer people sick at once is how a ward copes. That's the point of the vaccine mandate. Yes from me.

New Haven's arts festival has put out 40 events, and somebody will be round asking to borrow the school's chairs. In 2021 our hall sat locked for months and I swept dust off a stage nobody stood on. I'd like this programme to actually go ahead for the whanau. Proof of vaccination is how a hall stays open through an outbreak, not how it gets shut. YES from me.

ferry delays again this week, which surprises nobody at the yard. old boats break. out on the islands the clinic is one nurse and a gp once a week, and the ferry or the chopper is how anyone sick gets to a hospital. not the time to let a new virus run loose. so the vaccine requirement gets a yes from me

No community spread here yet. Good. That's the window. You back up the phone before it goes in the harbour, not after. In 2021 I ran repairs out of my car boot to cover the kiosk lease. Not doing a sequel. Get ready while it's quiet. Voting yes 🙃

People worry this would split the island in two. The split I saw in 2021 was at the hospital. Wards full of covid, operations put off for months, and my regulars at the counter asking for something stronger for the pain while they waited. A full hospital lets everyone down, vaccinated or not. Keeping it from filling up is the fairest thing we can do. Voting YES.

For some towns on the ring road, my van is the whole library. When it was parked up through 2021, my regulars went without, the older ones most of all. The rule that worries people is what keeps the van, the school and the corner shop going if the virus does arrive. Nobody along that road gets left out of a lockdown that never happens. Yes from me, come voting day.

The doctors are asking us to get ready before this virus spreads here, not after. Last time we waited, and my wife, whose lungs are not strong, lived in the storeroom behind our counter for months. I would much rather we prepare while it is quiet. I shall be voting yes.

The week my neighbour's lad was in intensive care in 2021 stays with me. Fit young bloke, worked the yards with his dad. There are only so many intensive-care beds on this island, around thirty in the whole country. I can count, and that's not many. I'd rather we get ahead of this one than fight over a bed. Yes from me in the vote, grudgingly.

ngl my first reaction was nah, nobody tells me what goes in my arm. not the trust-the-government sort, never will be. then i actually read the proposal. jab's free, nothing starts till all of us have had the chance to get it, under 12s exempt, medical exemptions too. no one's getting forced. still rate my freedom. yes from me

Centre shut in 2021 and my kiosk went with it. A shut centre pays nobody. Not the cleaners, not the food court, not me. A vaccine certificate weighs a lot less than a padlock on the whole building. Ticking yes.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Every lunch rush half of Crown Harbour comes through our restaurant, and I don't get to choose who. If a vaccine makes a hospital bed less likely for me and my kitchen while we keep feeding people, I'll have it. Nobody on my staff gets pushed into it either. Mine's a yes vote.
topic: Work and jobs (NO's "people unable to work")

text: Kids under twelve are exempt from the requirement, so the little ones won't need any proof. Yet they lost more than anyone when the schools shut in 2021. I walked those empty corridors most days and I know which ones never really came back. Keeping classrooms open comes first for me. Come the referendum, I'll be ticking yes.

2021 took every gig i had. a couple of the old crew sold their gear and never played again, and you don't get those years back. i want a full summer of hotel bars and open mics, the whole room singing the wrong words. getting ahead of this virus beats another shutdown. voting yes

In 2021 the elderly people I visit went months without seeing their families, and some never saw them again. I took funerals where only ten could stand at the graveside. What keeps a rest home open to visitors is less virus going round outside it. That is all this vote means to me. For their sake, I'll be voting yes.

Half my 6am customers are nurses coming off nights at Central, and they look done in. Central is still 40 nurses short. In 2021 the wards ran over capacity and that lot carried it. If a vaccine requirement keeps those wards from overflowing again, I'm all for it. Yes from me.

In 2021 the hotel stood me down for most of the year. I sent Mama what little I had, and some weeks it was nothing. Now I am back in the kitchen for breakfast rush every morning, tired, naku, but working. A free vaccine is honestly small next to another year like that. So I am a yes po.

My kids missed a year of swimming lessons in 2021. On an island. The pool shut with everything else. They're back in the water now and I'd like it to stay that way. A vaccine requirement beats another closure. Voting yes.

Plenty of people at my counter are wary of a brand-new mRNA jab, and that doesn't make anyone silly. I was too, so I read up. In the trials it meant less serious illness, and no major safety problems have shown up so far. The first doses go to health workers and people at high risk, voluntarily. The vote is about proof for shared places; getting the jab stays your own call. I'm a yes.
topic: Vaccine doubts (settle a worry, grant nothing)

text: As a migrant worker I worry about my papers more than most. So I read the fine print. Proof would be a certificate from the health ministry, on paper or digital. It is separate from the national ID card. The law for that card does not allow health records on it. I was nervous about new rules too. Still, I am voting yes.
topic: Privacy and ID card (settle a worry)

text: In the season, plenty of the people buying sunscreen and cold drinks at our store are visitors from Australia and New Zealand. An outbreak in high season would empty the hotels faster than any certificate could. Visitors' own recognised certificates would be accepted. I would like the island open and my customers well. I will be voting yes.

Took the van round the ring road towns this week, and chat after chat was someone still making up their mind. It's a big decision and they're taking it seriously. Mine came down to a woman out there who can't get to Central in a hurry. For her sake I'm ticking yes in the vote.
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: quiet week at the yard. boss had us sorting gear for the wet season now instead of halfway through it. that's how i see this vote. the doctors reckon you get ready before a virus is spreading, not after. you patch the hull while it's dry. yes from me
topic: Before Poll 2: deadlock, no NO lead

text: My son was eleven in 2021 and did his schoolwork at a table in our takeaway kitchen, between orders. No friends over, no football. I don't want that again for him or anyone's kids. A free vaccine and a certificate is a trade I'll take. Voting yes.

Flour's up again, the oven's on its last legs, and I'm doing the sums at 4am. Bakeries are a gamble at the best of times. Another closure is one more bad card in the hand. Last time I was takeaway-only for a year. I'd take a vaccine certificate over that any day. Yes from me.
